faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.body: The short version of what people ask before they start clipping offline.

sources.question: What videos can I clip?
sources.answer: Files on your computer (MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, MP3, WAV) always work offline. Pasting a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link also works, but downloading it needs the internet.

selection.question: How does ClipWright Studio choose the clips?
selection.answer: It transcribes the audio word by word with a local Whisper model, then a local Ollama model reads the whole transcript and picks moments that stand on their own. Each one is scored for hook, engagement, value, and shareability, and you can trim, split, or merge any clip afterwards.

minutes.question: Is there a usage limit?
minutes.answer: No. ClipWright Studio runs on your hardware, so there are no minute allowances or plans. Very long sources are limited only by your disk space and patience for CPU rendering.

publishing.question: Can ClipWright Studio post to TikTok and Instagram?
publishing.answer: Not offline. Clipping, editing, captioning and rendering work with no connection at all; connecting a social account and uploading a post needs the internet and is opt-in.

watermark.question: Do clips have a watermark?
watermark.answer: No. ClipWright Studio never adds a watermark.

languages.question: Does it work in other languages?
languages.answer: Yes. Whisper detects the spoken language automatically, so transcripts, captions, and clip picks follow the language of the video.

selfHost.question: Does it need a GPU or an API key?
selfHost.answer: No. It runs on CPU with local Whisper and Ollama, and no AI API key is required. Hosted AI providers stay available but disabled unless you turn them on.

cancel.question: Can I use it without an account?
cancel.answer: The app is yours: it runs locally with its own database. Accounts exist only to keep projects separate on a shared machine.
